rows.fidelity_note: The potential condition requires four nonnegative bounds and finite squared-integral estimates for the first potential, the second potential’s gradient and the flux. The remainder estimate is a separate condition using its nonnegative proposed bound.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNorms

rows.fidelity_note: The remainder condition requires a nonnegative bound, measurability and a finite integral of |y|²|R|² bounded by (ρ/2)². The factor one half and the sign condition are both explicit.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.RemainderBounded

rows.fidelity_note: The potential contribution is the square root of a sum containing the squared combined gradient, flux and remainder bound divided by w. The formula itself imposes no positive-weight premise.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.potentialDefect

rows.fidelity_note: The pin contribution adds the approximation error to the coefficient norm times the rounding error divided by √w. Positive weight comes from the surrounding certificate assumptions.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEntry.pinCharge

rows.fidelity_note: The central residual includes the pressure gradient and subtracts the gradient of |W|²/2. Removing that subtraction changes the residual being bounded.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.centreDefect

rows.fidelity_note: The linear residual includes the tangent pressure gradient and subtracts the gradient of the central–tangent inner product. This is the kinetic cross term required by the pressure correction.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.linearDefect

rows.fidelity_note: The offset data store constant, linear and quadratic coefficient arrays and error bounds. Their upper-triangular interpretation and the combination of ordered quadratic terms are imposed by separate formulas and conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.OffsetExpansionEntry

rows.fidelity_note: This row computes one ordered quadratic residual contribution. Combining both orders off the diagonal and summing only upper-triangular pairs occur in other rows.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.OffsetExpansionEntry.orderedQuadratic

rows.fidelity_note: The quadratic coefficient keeps one ordered term on the diagonal and adds both ordered terms off the diagonal. The offset sum separately restricts these coefficients to upper-triangular index pairs.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.OffsetExpansionEntry.quadraticCoefficient

rows.fidelity_note: A single decomposition R=R₁+R₂ must satisfy both component bounds and the sum of their budgets. The free-direction estimate separately chooses one family of dual bounds valid for every parameter.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.DualBounded

rows.fidelity_note: The radial spectral factor contains the inverse cell-width square and uses j(j+2) on the axis or j(j+1) off it. Positive width is supplied by cell validity.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialEigen

rows.fidelity_note: The height spectral factor is l(l+1) times the squared reciprocal half-height. The formula remains defined at zero height, so its geometric use needs the separate positive-height condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.heightEigen

rows.fidelity_note: The projection selects a polynomial satisfying all weighted orthogonality equations when such a polynomial exists and returns zero otherwise. Agreement with a computed least-squares solution needs existence and uniqueness on the intended space.

rows.fidelity_note: The tail norm is the weighted squared norm after subtracting that selected projection. It inherits the projection’s zero fallback until the projection conditions are established.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.tailNormSq

rows.fidelity_note: The test combination multiplies each real test by the complex conjugate of its coefficient. The inverse-Gram estimate and its positivity premise are separate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.testCombination

rows.fidelity_note: The trace-data map multiplies the complex trace vector by the prescribed real matrix. Its entries and ordering must agree with the matrix used in the subsequent complex quadratic estimate.

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.turnVector

rows.plain: Angular derivative in a moving frame

rows.fidelity_note: The radial and height columns are the corresponding meridian derivatives, while the angular column is the moving-frame angular derivative divided by r. Smoothness at r=0 requires separate conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testGrad
rows.plain: Gradient of a harmonic test field

rows.fidelity_note: Solenoidality is an exact weighted divergence identity throughout the closed cell rectangle. It is a separate condition from the formula for the angular derivative.

rows.fidelity_note: The reconstructed low gradient uses degrees zero through Q in both meridian coordinates and retains its harmonic and two component indices. The other coordinate blocks are not part of this reconstruction.

rows.fidelity_note: The leaf energy is block diagonal on the resolved harmonic coordinates and zero on the added port and actuator blocks. The complete cell index still retains those distinct added blocks.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.energyLeafForm

rows.fidelity_note: The mode-layout data store a layout, a coordinate parametrization and selected relations for every label. They impose no positive boundary-degree or valid-layout requirement.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellModeLayouts

rows.fidelity_note: Layout validity requires boundary degree at least one on every resolved label and identifies the local volume and boundary degrees with the mesh. The stronger tested-mode degree condition comes from mesh validity.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellModeLayouts

rows.fidelity_note: The test-shape formula uses component-dependent degrees q or q−1, with natural-number subtraction. It contains no positive-q premise, so the active mesh and layout guards remain necessary.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsTestOfShape

rows.fidelity_note: The radial polynomial weight switches on the exact equality r₁=0. The axis and off-axis bases therefore remain distinct even when a positive radius is very small.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.radialBeta

rows.fidelity_note: The side radius is r₁ for side zero and r₂ for every other side. The assembled formula must therefore call it only with the intended radial-side restriction.

rows.fidelity_note: The height-side selector gives the lower endpoint for side two and the upper endpoint otherwise. Its fallback does not make a radial side into a height face.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideHeightIndex

rows.fidelity_note: The radial-side selector gives the inner endpoint for side zero and the outer endpoint otherwise. It is used under the radial-side restriction in the assembled formula.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideRadialIndex

rows.fidelity_note: The face row branches explicitly between radial sides zero and one and height sides two and three. Each branch uses its own endpoint selectors, angular factors and boundary orientation.

rows.fidelity_note: The strain face row uses the same radial-versus-height side convention and its orientation. Its component selectors must be interpreted on the side for which the row is assembled.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.strainFaceRow

rows.fidelity_note: The curl formula contracts the alternating sign with the gradient entry whose output index is last and derivative index is first in that contraction. This preserves the stated output-first storage convention for the gradient array.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlComp

rows.fidelity_note: The packed vector places gradient entry (a,b) at 3a+b and then the three velocity components at indices nine through eleven. A transpose or a different packing order changes this vector.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.pairVec

rows.fidelity_note: The sesquilinear form conjugates the first vector and sums against the full 12 by 12 complex matrix and the second vector. The gradient/velocity packing is supplied by the vectors passed to this formula.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.matrixSesq

rows.fidelity_note: The vector moment condition requires exact cancellation against every monomial up to the supplied bidegree, for every harmonic and component, using ordinary meridian measure. The active degree 2d+1 and the separate long-mode exclusion come from surrounding conditions.

rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsMatOrthogonal

rows.fidelity_note: The basis data provide radial and height coefficients at every pair of natural indices. Positive leading coefficients and orthonormality belong to the separate validity condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBases

rows.fidelity_note: The radial polynomial at degree j uses the supplied coefficients through degree j. The formula allows every natural j, while positivity and orthonormality require the separate basis condition.

rows.fidelity_note: The height polynomial at degree l uses the supplied coefficients through degree l. Its intended basis properties must hold for the full family, beyond any finite stored prefix.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBases.heightPoly

rows.fidelity_note: Validity requires positive leading coefficients at every natural degree and exact radial and height orthonormality for every pair of degrees. An all-zero continuation would violate those requirements.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBases

rows.fidelity_note: The face data contain a test-coefficient function at every pair of natural indices. Nonzero leading coefficients are an additional validity condition on this entire family.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegment

rows.fidelity_note: The test of degree d is the polynomial formed from coefficients zero through d. Nothing in this evaluation formula guarantees a nonzero leading coefficient.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegment.test

rows.fidelity_note: A valid face requires distinct opposite levels, ordered interval endpoints and a nonzero leading test coefficient at every natural degree. The last condition excludes an all-zero continuation.

ties.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testSupForm

rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testSupForm
rows.plain: Form from an inverse Gram matrix

rows.fidelity_note: The test matrix consists of the exact weighted integrals of products of the supplied tests over the cell. Its construction alone does not establish positive definiteness.

rows.fidelity_note: The inner-height form uses differentiated weighted monomial tests and the inverse of their matching Gram matrix. Its variational interpretation requires the accompanying validity hypotheses.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInnerForm

rows.fidelity_note: The outer-radial form uses its prescribed boundary rows and their radial-weighted test Gram matrix. The inverse must refer to that exact matrix and ordering.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterForm

rows.fidelity_note: The outer-height form uses the stated boundary rows and the radial-weighted monomial Gram matrix with its own degree ranges. Its inverse is meaningful for the estimate only under the accompanying validity hypotheses.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOuterForm

rows.fidelity_note: The axis angular form uses its specific angular tests and their radial-weighted Gram matrix. Those tests and that matrix must remain paired when evaluating the inverse form.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularAxisForm

rows.fidelity_note: This expression is the real quadratic form of the inverse of the supplied complex matrix. The expression alone does not establish positive definiteness or invertibility.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.inverseWeightedSq

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.LeafValues
ties.plain: Coefficients of a resolved cell leaf

rows.fidelity_note: The leaf data store a 12 by 12 complex matrix at every label and meridian point, together with proposed scalar bounds. They impose neither Hermiticity nor inequalities on all complex vectors.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.LeafValues
rows.plain: Coefficients of a resolved cell leaf

rows.fidelity_note: The local form integrates the full complex matrix against the packed gradient/velocity basis vectors and keeps different harmonics separate. Hermiticity and the all-vector comparison are separate requirements.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowSlotForm

rows.fidelity_note: The mode block adds the derivative-energy form to the integrated local complex form. It uses the complete packed gradient/velocity matrix, whose validity is required elsewhere.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.modeBlockForm

rows.fidelity_note: The top-degree expression uses natural-number subtraction, so Q−1 equals zero at Q=0. The active layout’s degree conditions govern where that expression is used.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.topForm

rows.fidelity_note: The off-axis angular weight is (r₂−r)/(r r₂). Positive radial denominators are supplied by the intended off-axis geometry.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOffWeight

rows.fidelity_note: The component form branches on the exact condition r₁=0 and chooses the axis or off-axis angular form accordingly. The inner radial and height contributions also depend on that branch.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.componentForm

rows.fidelity_note: The curl coefficient adds an angular gain divided by r². Positive radius is an external geometric requirement; this formula does not contain the splitting-length or exterior conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.curlWithGain

rows.fidelity_note: The gradient floor combines the curl coefficient with a Hessian angular gain divided by r². Its intended point test therefore retains the positive-radius domain.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gradFloor

rows.fidelity_note: The shifted velocity coefficient adds the shift times the angular gain divided by r². Its formula alone imposes no sign or positive-radius requirement.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.velWithShift

rows.fidelity_note: The point test requires nonnegative Hessian and shift, nonnegative remaining diagonal coefficients and the cross-term discriminant comparison. Positive radius and the other denominator conditions are supplied by the enclosing geometric assumptions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.PassesTest

rows.fidelity_note: The charge coverage condition uses the stated point coefficients on their prescribed domain. Its interval interpretation must retain the positive-radius and positive-denominator assumptions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.EntryCharges.Covers

rows.fidelity_note: The operator comparison holds for every complex vector and uses the square of the proposed bound. Consequently this condition by itself is unchanged when that bound changes sign.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.opBound

rows.fidelity_note: The mean-gradient clause uses that squared complex operator comparison, while the other clauses bound real strain and wave gradients. This condition does not itself add nonnegativity of every charge.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsChargeBound

rows.fidelity_note: This condition supplies positivity for auxiliary box constants and comparisons with model-error costs. It neither defines the squared operator comparison nor asserts nonnegativity of every charge in that comparison.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafBoxLink

rows.fidelity_note: The layout data preserve optional references for segment endpoints and cell corners. The rules governing when a reference may be absent are separate validity conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout

rows.fidelity_note: An absent corner produces the zero stream row, while a present corner selects its coordinate. This evaluation rule does not establish that the absence is geometrically allowed.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.streamAt

rows.fidelity_note: The zero harmonic is returned only when it belongs to the selected mode set; otherwise it is absent. This membership decision must be preserved independently of corner-coordinate rules.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.zeroMode

rows.fidelity_note: Layout validity restricts absent segment endpoints and cell corners to the stated axis cases and ties present references to exact geometric points. The zero-valued lookup formulas do not replace those requirements.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsCellLayout
rows.plain: Geometry and tests of a layout

rows.fidelity_note: A corner lookup distinguishes absence from a present coordinate. The accompanying axis rules determine when that absence is allowed.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.cornerAt

rows.fidelity_note: The gradient coordinate is selected only when both degrees are at most Q; otherwise the row is zero. Those zero values must not be mistaken for valid stored coordinates.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.strainAt

rows.fidelity_note: The velocity coordinate is selected only when both degrees are strictly below Q; otherwise the row is zero. Its valid range is smaller than the gradient range.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.velocityAt

rows.fidelity_note: The auxiliary side-velocity coordinate is selected only for degree at most Q and is zero outside that range. The harmonic, side and component indices remain part of the selected coordinate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.extraAt

rows.fidelity_note: The split condition bounds the full field minus its model, high and long parts at every point of the supplied solid and every time. The specialized application supplies the owned positive-radius portion of a cell.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitPart

rows.fidelity_note: The almost-everywhere split places one meridian exceptional set outside all time and angle quantifiers. The owned positive-radius cell portion is supplied separately as its solid.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitPartAE

rows.fidelity_note: The supremum loss contains a velocity-square term divided by the splitting length. The later strict positivity hypothesis is what permits its Young-inequality interpretation.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremumLoss

rows.fidelity_note: The gradient row integrates with radial measure and conjugates the test gradient, including the stated dilation term. Boundary orientation signs occur in the separate side rows.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownStrainRow

rows.fidelity_note: The velocity row uses radial measure and the conjugated test polynomial, multiplied by i times the frequency plus one half. It contains no boundary-orientation factor.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownVelocityRow

rows.fidelity_note: The gradient side row carries the negative outward edge sign, conjugates the test moment and includes the side radius on radial faces. This sign is opposite to the pressure side row.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideGradRow

rows.fidelity_note: The pressure side row carries the positive outward edge sign and uses the normal test component with the appropriate radial-face factor. It conjugates the same kind of side moment.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sidePresRow

rows.fidelity_note: The assembled own row places the gradient, velocity, gradient-side and pressure-side formulas in their respective coordinate blocks and makes the remaining blocks zero. Their different boundary signs are preserved through that assembly.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownRowVector

rows.fidelity_note: The gradient coupling row integrates the displayed alternating-symbol products with radial measure and a conjugated test component. Boundary pressure and gradient rows are separate terms of the own row.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.couplingStrainRow

rows.fidelity_note: The velocity coupling row integrates the alternating-symbol product of the conjugated test and vorticity with radial measure. It carries no independent side-orientation term.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.couplingVelocityRow

rows.fidelity_note: The coupling vector places its gradient and velocity coupling rows in their two blocks and sets all remaining blocks to zero. Side-gradient and pressure contributions belong to the separate own row.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.couplingRowVector

rows.fidelity_note: The parametrization data store the ordered relation matrix, chosen solved-coordinate map and retained boundary-coordinate set. Injectivity and invertibility are separate requirements on exactly these data.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.ParamData

rows.fidelity_note: The solved block consists of the relation matrix columns selected by the solved-coordinate map, in that order. Invertibility of another ordered submatrix would not establish invertibility of this block.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.ParamData.solvedBlock

rows.fidelity_note: Validity requires an injective solved-coordinate map, disjointness from the retained boundary coordinates and invertibility of the selected square block. Those conditions refer to the same stored selection.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsParamData

rows.fidelity_note: The edge sign is positive when the opposite level lies below the selected level and negative otherwise. Distinct levels are required separately for the trace formula.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.edgeSign

rows.fidelity_note: The radial strip moment retains both the edge sign and the signed denominator c−o. Replacing that denominator by its absolute value without adjusting the sign changes the formula.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialStripMoment

rows.fidelity_note: The height strip moment also uses the edge sign and signed denominator c−o, together with the supplied radial weight. The nonzero-separation condition is external to this expression.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.heightStripMoment

rows.fidelity_note: The face moment selects the radial or height strip formula according to the side direction, retaining the stored opposite level. The height branch additionally uses the prescribed weighted or unweighted radial measure.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegment.moment

rows.fidelity_note: The eight coordinate blocks give the displayed cardinality, with the single stream-corner block outside the harmonic factor. The gradient, velocity, side and pressure blocks retain their different degree cutoffs.

rows.fidelity_note: The layout’s coordinate family is obtained by substituting its harmonic set and stored degrees and counts into those eight blocks. The stream-corner block is consequently counted only once.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.Datum

rows.fidelity_note: This row establishes finiteness of that exact eight-block coordinate family. Its cardinality is the displayed sum of block sizes, including the unmultiplied stream-corner count.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.instFintypeDatum

rows.fidelity_note: This row indexes the relation equations, whereas the displayed cardinality counts local data coordinates. The two families have different blocks and the cardinality formula does not describe this row.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.RelIndex

rows.fidelity_note: The velocity-tail gain is the minimum of the radial and height spectral factors at degree Q. Both factors vanish at Q=0, so positive gain requires the active degree and geometry assumptions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.velTailGain

rows.fidelity_note: This row is only the nonnegative velocity charge, obtained by taking the positive part of the sum of three costs. The zero-degree gain and division by that gain occur in the surrounding tail-budget formula.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.velCharge

rows.plain: A vertical trace moment at z=0

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.SignedTree

rows.fidelity_note: This row requires one measurable homogeneous radius R with 0<R₀≤R≤R₁. The square-exterior alternative and its zero-angular-frequency requirement occur in the exterior condition, so they are context beyond this row.

rows.fidelity_note: The omitted-mode data contain potentially infinite mode and spatial sets, a spatial shift function and coefficient bounds. A finite encoding must specify their meanings on the full domains.
